r: A **socio-economic and ritual** arrangement in which one caste secures the services of another; everyone works for a family or group to which he is **hereditarily** linked – at once economic, political and socio-cultural
The castes rendering hereditary services; paid in kind (grain share) at harvest
**Functional interdependence** of castes, **hereditary** ties, **inequality** of status between groups
Beidelman calls it exploitative; "feudalism" is not a defining feature
Rested on **dominance and reciprocity** (patron dominance + exchange of services)
A **caste-village** system; economic exchange **between tribes** is mainly **barter**
Andhra: **12** hereditary functionaries paid by Manyam land or harvest share
Varnas from head, arms, thighs, feet
**Abbé J.A. Dubois** (*Hindu Manners, Customs and Ceremonies*, 19th c.)
Caste **saved Hindu society from barbarism**; also wrote that a Hindu woman could go anywhere alone without fear of insult
Credited with first using the word **"untouchable"** for these castes; the colonial term was "Depressed Classes"
Early Vedic: no rigid varna; **Later Vedic**: four hereditary varnas crystallise; **post-Maurya/Gupta**: Manu Smriti, rigid caste
Brought rigidity, inequality and exclusion rather than perfect social stability
Caste is an **extended (broad) kinship group** – jatis grew from separate tribal/kin groups
*History of Caste in India* (1909): membership by **birth** + bar on marrying outside
Common name, claimed mythical ancestor, same hereditary calling; **ranked castes in the 1901 Census**; first to define caste scientifically
Caste developed through social and religious disabilities
Ranking by exchange of **"coded substances"** (food, water, services)

Segmental division; hierarchy; restrictions on feeding and social intercourse; civil and religious disabilities and privileges; **lack of free choice of occupation**; restrictions on marriage (endogamy)
Enunciated **seven cultural traits** of caste (endogamy, commensal and food restrictions, hereditary occupation, pollution, etc.)
Pollution by touch, untouchability, Sanskritic rituals, commensal taboos

**4,147** castes; caste enumeration began with the **1871** Census

**Ashraf** (foreign descent, upper-caste converts), **Ajlaf** (clean occupational groups), **Arzal** (lowest; converts from untouchable castes)
